question.text: A linearly polarised electromagnetic wave in vacuum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>cos</mi><mfenced open="[" close="]"><mrow><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is incident normally on a perfectly reflecting wall at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>. Choose the correct option.

options.text: The frequency of electromagnetic wave is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>54</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>.

The transmitted wave will be
3.1cos1.8z-5.4×106ti^ N/C.

The reflected wave will be
3.1cos1.8z+5.4×106ti^ N C-1.

solution.text: Reflected wave will have direction opposite to incident wave.
